definition: The region of the input that influences a given neuron's output.
details: The region of the input that influences a given neuron's output. Deep stacks of convolutions grow the receptive field gradually; attention gives every token a global receptive field in one layer.

explainer.lead: A unit's receptive field is the slice of input that can change its output. It sets what context a neuron can possibly see, so it governs how much information each layer has access to.

tiers.eli5: Like how far a security guard can see from their post: anything outside that range never reaches them.
tiers.practitioner: Architects stack convolutions to grow the receptive field gradually, or use attention to give every token a global one in a single layer. A pitfall is assuming a unit sees more context than it does, so information outside its field is invisible to it.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the region of the input that influences a given neuron's output. Deep convolution stacks expand it gradually; one attention layer gives every token a global receptive field.

explainer.example: In a deep CNN, early layers respond to small edges while later layers respond to whole objects, because their receptive fields have grown through stacking.
